sources.supports: Roles of lenses, aperture, shutter and recording surface in image formation. Our assembly is a schematic abstraction, not a replica.

scenes.title: Take the camera apart.
text: Start by separating the parts. The arrangement becomes easier to read when the lens, aperture, shutter and recording plane no longer overlap. Select each part to connect its position with its job. You are looking at an original teaching model, not a scan of a particular camera: its distances and shapes simplify a functional relationship.

Before moving on, trace the route from the lens towards the recording plane. The lens changes directions, the opening limits the bundle, the shutter controls exposure and the final surface records light. Each role answers a different question. A convincing model is useful only if it helps you keep those roles distinct.

scenes.title: Watch the shutter open.
scenes.deck: One motion makes the shutter’s role visible.
text: Press Play to watch the shutter plate move aside and return. The lens, aperture ring and recording plane stay where they are. The contrast makes one role visible: the shutter controls an interval during which the recording surface can receive light. Drag to look from another angle, or move the cycle slider to hold a particular position.

This original schematic uses a sliding plate to make the relationship clear. It does not reproduce the mechanism of a particular camera, and its slow eight-second cycle is for observation rather than an exposure setting. Forming an image, limiting the opening and controlling the exposure interval remain different operations. The next view returns to the ideal lens and the geometry of focusing.

scenes.title: Move the object. Find its image.
scenes.deck: Move the object. Find its image.
text: The object arrow is drawn on one side of a converging lens. Two representative rays make the geometry visible. Change object distance while keeping focal length fixed, then compare the position and direction of the image arrow. The diagram draws a few explanatory rays, not every light ray in the scene.

Try Object at 2F as a reference configuration. Then bring the object towards the focal point. Watch the calculated image distance as well as the drawing: an image can move outside the available canvas. The panel tells you when this happens, so a missing arrow does not have to become a mystery or a rendering trick.

scenes.title: What happens inside the focus?
text: Now put the object closer than one focal length. The emerging rays do not meet on the far side of this lens. Their backward extensions identify a virtual image. The dotted construction is a way of locating the apparent origin of the rays; light is not travelling backwards along those dotted lines.

Switch between the three configurations and describe what changed before looking for a rule. The numerical sign is meaningful: a positive image distance belongs beyond the lens in this convention, while a negative value identifies the object side. At the exact focus the model has no finite image plane, so the interface reports that state explicitly.

scenes.title: Return to the recording plane.
text: Return to the assembly and select the recording plane. You can now ask a more precise question than whether the camera contains a good lens: does the recording surface coincide with the image formed for this object? Separating parts is an explanatory gesture here; it does not operate a real focusing mechanism.

Section view clips the supplied geometry so overlapping components are easier to compare. It cannot discover an interior that the model does not contain. This distinction matters whenever an attractive visualization seems to explain a physical object: the represented structure, the calculation and the real device have related but different levels of detail.

scenes.title: An image is a relationship.
text: You have connected a visible assembly with an experiment you can change. The purpose of the model was not to memorize the shape of this camera. It was to distinguish component roles and recognize how object position, focal length and recording position work together.

Keep the idealizations in view when taking this explanation further. Real lenses have thickness, aberrations and other behavior absent from the thin-lens construction. You can return to either workbench, reopen the sources or ask a more specific question. The parts and controls remain tools for reasoning, not evidence that this diagram represents every camera.

assembly.description: Original schematic of a simple camera: a converging lens, aperture, shutter and recording plane. Geometry is intentionally simplified, with arbitrary drawing units, no manufacturer dimensions and no claim that all cameras have this arrangement. Separation is an explanatory view, not a disassembly procedure.

parts.label: Lens
parts.explanation: A real lens changes the direction of light. This simplified cylinder marks its position; the next experiment models the focusing action with rays. Its displayed thickness is illustrative.

parts.label: Aperture
parts.explanation: The aperture limits the bundle of light passing through. The open ring represents a stop; this 3D view does not calculate depth of field or diffraction.

parts.label: Shutter
parts.explanation: The shutter controls when the recording surface is exposed. This plate represents a closed shutter; its operating mechanism is omitted.

parts.label: Recording plane
parts.explanation: Light must form a useful image at the recording plane. A digital sensor measures it; film records it chemically. This plate identifies the plane, not the microscopic sensor structure.

motion.description: The shutter slides aside to uncover the recording plane, then closes again. The lens and aperture stay still. This is a slowed-down schematic, not a real exposure setting.

cues.label: Closed
cues.explanation: The plate sits in front of the recording plane.

cues.label: Opening
cues.explanation: The shutter plate moves aside. The lens and recording plane stay in place.

cues.label: Open
cues.explanation: The plate is clear of the recording plane for this part of the cycle.

cues.label: Closing
cues.explanation: The plate returns to cover the recording plane.

cues.label: Closed again
cues.explanation: The cycle ends with the recording plane covered again.
